title: Protocol for constructing a versatile tiling light sheet microscope for imaging cleared tissues
protocol: Install the Windows 10 professional 64-bit operating system on the control workstation for the microscope.
Install the NI PCIe-6323 control board and its device driver.
Install the camera frame grabber and its device driver.
Install Labview 2019 developer suite or a later version.
Install Matlab 2019a or a later version.
Install the vendor provided control software for optoelectrical components.
Install device drivers for laser sources, SLM, PI translation stages, filter wheel, and detection camera.
Confirm proper functioning of all devices using vendor provided control software.
Install custom main control software from key resources table.
Install phase map generation software from key resources table.
Install image reconstruction software from key resources table.
Connect the control workstation to SH-68A connector blocks with SHC68-68-EPM shielded cables.
Connect microscope optoelectrical devices to assigned analog outputs, digital inputs, and digital outputs of SH-68A connector blocks with BNC cables.
Ensure all optoelectrical components can be controlled with main control software.
Construct the optomechanical system of the microscope.
Combine and collimate excitation continuous wave (CW) laser beams.
Install laser sources and laser combiner on optical table according to microscope design.
Combine all CW laser beams into a single coincident beam before the expanding and collimating lenses L1 (f=30 mm) and L2 (f=200 mm).
Align the rest of the microscope using the 488 nm CW laser.
Expand and collimate the combined laser beam using lenses L1 and L2.
Note: Ensure the collimation of the 488 nm laser beam with a shear interferometer.
Inspect the collimation of other laser beams.
Install the polarizing beamsplitter (PBS) assembly on the optical table according to the design.
Ensure the collimated laser beam from the PBS incidents vertically at the center of the SLM liquid crystal surface.
Rotate the half wave plate HWP1 to maximize the intensity of transmitted light through the PBS.
Install the galvanometer assembly on the optical table according to the design.
Center the galvo rotating axis to the reference mounting hole on the optical table using the XY translation stage.
Install the optical slit assembly.
Conjugate the galvo mirror to the SLM through relay lenses L4 (f=175 mm) and L3 (f=300 mm).
Install lens L4 first without lens L3.
Direct the reflected collimated laser beam from the SLM through lens L4.
Adjust the position of lens L4 until the laser beam focuses on the galvo mirror.
Install lens L3.
Adjust lens L3 by evaluating the collimation of the laser beam after lens L4.
Align lens L3 if the collimated laser beam remains collimated after passing through both lenses L3 and L4.
Apply a phase map with zero tiling phase to the SLM using the provided software.
Ensure the SLM stays on for further alignment.
Readjust the SLM position to conjugate the SLM liquid crystal surface with the galvo mirror.
Adjust the optical slit along the excitation light optical axis to locate it at the back focal plane of lens L3.
Rotate half wave plate HWP2 to maximize the intensity of the +1 and −1 diffraction orders of the laser beam.
Adjust the tilting angle of the SLM to let either the +1 or −1 diffraction order fall on the center of the optical slit.
Adjust the width of the optical slit to enable complete transmission of the selected diffraction order while blocking other diffraction orders.
Conjugate the galvo mirror to the rear pupil of the excitation objectives.
Adjust the rotating axis of the galvo mirror and ensure the excitation laser beam reflected by the galvo mirror is parallel to the optical table.
Install the prism mirror assembly.
Adjust prism mirrors PM1 and PM2 to ensure the laser beams reflected by both prism mirrors are parallel to the optical table.
Install the relay lens assemblies according to the design.
Install the excitation objective assemblies according to the design.
Conjugate the galvo mirror to the rear pupil of both excitation objectives through two relay lens assemblies respectively.
Adjust the lateral position of the excitation objectives.
Ensure the excitation laser beam is centered at the rear pupil of both excitation objectives.
Maintain the same propagation direction for the excitation beams as they enter each excitation objective.
Install the fluorescence detection assembly according to the design.
Use a piece of coordinate paper as the alignment target.
Place the coordinate paper under the detection objective in parallel to the optical table.
Focus the detection camera on the alignment target with ambient light.
Adjust the magnification by rotating the magnification knob on the MVX10 microscope body.
Ensure the alignment target is in focus within the field of view (FOV) at different magnifications.
Place a steel shim under the detection assembly mounting base if the alignment target is not in focus everywhere within the FOV.
Adjust the position of the steel shim until the alignment target is in focus within the FOV.
Install the imaging chamber assembly.
Fill the imaging chamber with the prepared dye solution.
Focus the microscope on the excitation beam without scanning the laser beam.

Readjust the axial position of both excitation objectives along the excitation light optical axis using the manual translation stages of the excitation objective assemblies to place the excitation beam waist at the center of the detection FOV.
Readjust the position of lens L6 along the excitation light optical axis.
Ensure conjugation between the galvo mirror and both excitation objectives.
Readjust the position of lens L8 along the excitation light optical axis.
Scan the excitation beam discretely within the field of view using the galvo mirror.
Readjust prism mirrors PM1 and PM2 if necessary to ensure focus at all positions within the FOV.
Replace the imaging chamber with another imaging chamber filled with an imaging buffer that matches the RI of the cleared tissue sample to be imaged.
Clean and dry an imaging chamber completely before filling it with a different kind of imaging buffer.
Install the sample translation assembly on the optical table according to the design.
Focus the detection camera on the sample holder using ambient light.
Move the sample holder in the horizontal directions and ensure the sample translation directions are coincident with the lateral directions of the detection FOV.
Calibrate the microscope for imaging cleared tissues using custom phase map generation software and main control software.
Fill the imaging chamber with an imaging buffer that matches the refractive index of the cleared tissue sample to be imaged.
Scan the excitation beam discretely to create a grid pattern in the imaging buffer using one of the excitation objectives.
Focus the microscope on the grid pattern.
Adjust the microscope magnification by adjusting the magnification knob on the MVX 10 microscope body based on the desired lateral spatial resolution.
Adjust the intensity profile of the excitation beam based on desired axial resolution and tiling number by changing illumination numerical apertures (NA) using the phase map generation program.
Find tiling coefficients and focus coefficients to tile the excitation beam on both sides of the detection FOV.
Keep the excitation beam in focus by adjusting the tiling coefficient and focusing coefficient using the phase map generation software.
Generate the phase maps used to tile the excitation beam within the FOV with the phase map generation software using calibrated coefficients.
Confirm the excitation beam is in focus at all tiling positions.
Repeat steps to calibrate all excitation wavelengths for multicolor imaging.
Generate corresponding phase maps using the phase map generation software.
Correct the focal position of the scanning excitation beam by changing the focusing coefficient.
Change the intensity profile of the scanning excitation beam by changing the illumination NAs (NAOD=0.05, NAID=0.015, NAOD=0.03, NAID=0.01, and NAOD=0.01, NAID=0).
Find the tiling coefficients to tile the light sheet at both sides of the FOV.
Generate two groups of phase maps to tile the excitation light sheet with the calibrated coefficients at 6 and 3 positions.
Load the generated phase maps.
Verify the tiling positions of the generated two groups of phase maps.
Mount the sample on the stainless steel sample holder.
Load the sample holder onto the sample translation stage.
Select regions of interest to be imaged using the main control program.
Start imaging the selected regions.
Adjust the excitation light sheet and tiling number using the phase map generation software.
Image the same sample volume with different spatial resolutions.
Verify differences in performance based on varying spatial resolutions.
Input the required parameters for image reconstruction, including tiling number and boundary positions between adjacent tiles.
Calculate amplitude masks to stitch raw images collected at different tiling positions.
Select raw image files to be reconstructed and start reconstructing.
Register and merge the reconstructed 3D images from adjacent sample volumes with Amira or other software.
